name: english_travel
input_text: At first I wanted to visit all the famous landmarks. The Eiffel Tower, Times Square, the Colosseum. I thought travel meant ticking off the big names everyone talks about. I would plan tight itineraries to see as many famous spots as possible. But after a few trips, something felt hollow. Standing in a crowd at a famous square, I realized I could not remember what I had actually enjoyed. The famous spots blurred together. What I remembered instead were the quiet moments. A small bookstore in a side street. A conversation with a local baker about morning routines. Watching the river alone at dawn before the city woke up. Those moments were not on any must-see list. Yet they were the ones that stayed with me. So I changed how I travel. I stopped chasing landmarks and started following curiosity. I look for quiet places where locals actually spend time. I prefer solo travel because it lets me notice details. I have learned that a good trip is not about how many famous places you see. It is about how deeply you connect with one ordinary place and the ordinary people who give it meaning.
